finalSummary.reviewScope: Only whether the new non-breakdown qualifier scopes this existing asymmetry/rectification summary was rechecked. Its other passing science and translation findings are inherited.

checks.subject: Explicit non-breakdown limit
checks.finding: The Chinese first sentence confines the lesson to reverse voltage insufficient to cause breakdown. English states the same limit. Neither relies on an undefined operating range.

checks.subject: Explained excluded case
checks.finding: Both second sentences explain that sufficiently large reverse voltage can produce a large reverse current, name that case reverse breakdown, and exclude it from the lesson. This is a qualitative, age-appropriate definition, not an invented numerical threshold or a claim that breakdown must permanently destroy the device.

checks.subject: Full prefix translation
checks.finding: English preserves both Chinese propositions, their reverse-voltage condition, possibility of large current, technical name and explicit exclusion. No qualifier, direction or magnitude distinction is lost or added.

checks.subject: Position before reversal comparison
checks.finding: The entire prefix occurs before the retained polarity reversal and equal-voltage-magnitude comparison. The later phrase operating range discussed in this lesson now has an explicit referent.

checks.subject: Scope through asymmetry and rectification
checks.finding: The wording limits the lesson's discussion, not merely a single current sentence. It therefore scopes the retained small minority-carrier reverse current, high reverse resistance, directional-asymmetry summary and suppression of reverse current during rectification. The final warning that rectified current can vary with time is unchanged.
